findings.summary: Undo of an Overlay switch reports "Undone: your earlier project is back, the one that started from ...", which overstates what Undo did.
findings.scenario: On the Overlays screen tick "Tooltip", then press Undo in the top bar (the screen's own hint at App.tsx:853 tells the owner to do this). In undo(), `touched` is empty (no Step value or Decision differs), `wholeProject` is false, and `small` only knows the name and the Contrast checks setting, so it is null. The text falls through to the `wholeProject || !first` branch at line 995-996 and says the whole earlier project is back. Only one Overlay changed. The comment at lines 990-991 names this exact overstatement as the thing `small` exists to prevent; the new `overlays` field was not added to it.
findings.suggestion: Add an overlays case to `small`: compare overlaysOf(now) with overlaysOf(previous) and say, for example, "Undone: the Overlay \"Tooltip\" is switched off again." Add an e2e assertion on the notice text.

findings.summary: hasWork() does not count switched-on Overlays, so a project whose only work is its Overlays is replaced without a question and without a kept copy.
findings.scenario: New project (plain start, default name). Go to #overlays and switch on three Overlays. On the Summary, open a project file: requestImport line 955 sees !hasWork and calls open() with no confirmation, and replaceKeepingCopy line 242 sees !worthKeeping and keeps no copy. The Overlay choices survive only in the Undo history, which a reload empties. The same project also reopens on the Directions screen (line 746) and the Directions screen shows no "Go on with my project" link (App.tsx:366 computes `started` the same way).
findings.suggestion: Let hasWork (or at least worthKeeping) also return true when overlaysOf(project).length > 0.

findings.summary: A skin chip is 32 pixels tall on a touch screen; the stylesheet's own touch rule (44 pixels for every control) does not list it.
findings.scenario: .skin has min-height: 2rem and its text is 0.8125rem, so each chip is 32px tall, with 6px gaps (.skin-row gap 0.375rem). The block `@media (pointer: coarse)` at lines 301-304 ("every control is at least 44 pixels tall") raises .btn, .check, .rail a and others to 2.75rem but not .skin. On a phone a Direction card shows up to about six chips in wrapped rows, each below the height that the Studio's own research rule 'target-size' (TARGET_MIN = 44) asks of the designs it produces.
findings.suggestion: Add `.skin` to the selector list at line 302 (min-height: 2.75rem under pointer: coarse).

findings.summary: On the Overlays screen the Rail's single Tab stop is the "Started from" link, not the link marked as the current page.
findings.scenario: The Rail is one Tab stop with arrow keys inside. On a Step the stop is the current Step (tab(here), line 466). On the Overlays screen no Step is `here`, so the stop falls to the first link (tab(s.view !== 'steps'), line 452), while the Overlays link carries aria-current="page" with tabIndex -1. A keyboard user who tabs into the Rail lands at the top and must press End, then ArrowUp, to reach the item that is marked current. Before this change the Rail was drawn only on Steps, so this branch never ran.
findings.suggestion: Give the Overlays link tabIndex={tab(s.view === 'overlays')} and the first link tab(false) in that case, so that the current item is the Tab stop on both screens.

findings.summary: The rule "Every button and link is at least 44 pixels tall" reports "Holds" from the constant token --target-min (always 2.75rem, tokens.ts:587), but the Mockup's own text links are set to 24 pixels.
findings.scenario: Any design: the Summary says "Holds. Buttons and links are at least 44 pixels tall." Yet packages/core/src/templates/smallBusiness.ts:239 gives `.actions .link, .service .more, address .phone, .nav-actions .phone` a `min-height: 1.5rem` (24 px), and `.brand` (line 196) has no minimum height at all. Only `.btn`, `.nav li a` and form controls use --target-min. The rule's `notChecked` text ("The Studio checks the height that the design gives to buttons and links") is also untrue for links. Because the token is a constant, no design can ever make this rule say "does not hold".
findings.suggestion: Either name the rule for what the token governs (buttons, menu links, form fields) and say in `found` that text links are 24 pixels, or raise the text links to --target-min. Do not present a constant as a measurement of "every" link.

findings.summary: A fade Skin on a Direction whose color strategy is quiet, tinted-surface or color-block loses its second color: the headline fades to a different hue than the Skin's `what` text states.
findings.scenario: skinParams applies `accent2Hue` only when the Direction is `duo` or `single-accent`, but always sets `displayTreatment: 'accent-gradient'`. For any other strategy tokens.ts:490 ends the fade at `shiftH(accentText, 52)`. Pairs the Catalog offers: "Sunset fade" ("Orange that fades into rose pink", 42 to 355) on graphite-precision, quiet-luxury, cobalt-wash, steady-steps fades from hue 42 to hue 94 (yellow-green). "Meadow fade" ("into yellow-green", 100) on graphite-precision, quiet-luxury, cobalt-wash ends at 192 (blue-green). "Orchid fade" ("into violet", 275) on paper-and-ink and steady-steps ends at 12 (red). The chip in App.tsx:313 shows one flat color for these pairs, because `second` is read only when the strategy is duo. Derived from the code; I did not render it (no browser run allowed). No unit test compares the fade's end with the Skin's second color.
findings.suggestion: Do not list fade Skins on Directions that cannot carry a second color, or carry the Skin's second hue into the fade for every strategy; add a test that the far end of --display-fill has the Skin's accent2Hue for every listed pair.

findings.summary: The line-length rule reports the constant --measure (always "65ch", tokens.ts:567) as "the widest line of reading text", but only two paragraph kinds use that token.
findings.scenario: smallBusiness.ts applies `max-width: var(--measure)` only to `.service p` (286) and `.about p` (346). The services intro paragraph sits in `.section-head { max-width: 46rem }` (281) at --text-base: 736 px wide at 17 px text is about 43 em, wider than 65ch for an ordinary sans face (roughly 72ch or more), and wider still at a smaller text size (13 px on the slider: about 57 em). The Summary still says "The widest line of reading text holds about 65 letters. Holds." No design can change the value, so the rule can never fail. Also, "ch" is the width of the digit 0, which is wider than an average letter, so 65ch holds more than 65 letters. The width in letters is my estimate, not measured.
findings.suggestion: Put the --measure cap on every reading paragraph (section-head p included), or word `found` as "Paragraphs in the services and about sections are capped at 65 character widths".

findings.summary: The size-step rule looks only at `scaleRatio`, so it reports "Holds" when two real text sizes are equal or under a tenth apart.
findings.scenario: (1) baseSize 13 (the bottom of the "Text size" slider, steps.ts:275), scaleRatio 1.25: tokens.ts:521-523 gives --text-sm = max(13, 11.57) = 13 px and --text-base = 13 px, the same size, and --text-xs = 12 px (8% smaller). The Summary says "Each text size is 25 percent larger than the size below it. Holds." With baseSize 14: 14 / 13 / 12, steps of 7.7% and 8.3%. (2) On a 320-pixel phone, --lede-size = min(--text-lg, 5.6vw) = 17.92 px against reading text of 17 px (the default): 5% apart; at baseSize 19 or more the lede is smaller than the reading text. The `found` sentence is also untrue below the reading size in every design (sm is 0.89 of base, about 12%, never the scale ratio).
findings.suggestion: Measure the ratios between the consecutive worked-out size tokens (xs, sm, base, lg, ...) and report the smallest; state in `notChecked` that the caps on narrow screens are not measured.

findings.summary: The strong-colors measure can only answer 1 or 2 against a maximum of 2, so the rule can never fail, and its count is wrong for some designs.
findings.scenario: `count = colorStrategy === 'duo' ? 2 : 1`, `holds = count <= 2`: true for every possible input, so the unit test that binds it (catalog.test.ts:531) cannot fail for this rule. Wrong counts: the "Graphite" Skin (accentChroma 0.02, "Almost no color") is reported as "The design uses one strong color"; a non-duo design with `displayTreatment: 'accent-gradient'` or the aurora atmosphere draws a second hue 52 or 48 degrees away (tokens.ts:490, 361) and is still reported as one. The cited record's own design move is "neutrals and one accent"; the limit of two is the Studio's own number and the text does not say so.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the rule (a number that cannot change is not a measure) or count hues actually emitted (accent, accent-2, fade end, atmosphere) with a chroma threshold, and say that the limit of two is the Studio's choice.

findings.summary: The new "overlays" part of a project file is missing from SECTIONS, so a fault in it refuses the whole file with "This is not a Refraction project file."
findings.scenario: A project file with `"overlays": "tooltip"` (a string, not a list), or a list with one identifier longer than 40 characters, or more than 40 entries: `projectSchema` (line 690) fails with path[0] = 'overlays'; `SECTIONS.find` (line 854) returns undefined; the owner is told the file is not a project file at all, although every other part names itself (finding U2-21's purpose). It is also inconsistent: an unknown identifier of 40 characters is dropped with a note, one of 41 characters loses the whole project.
findings.suggestion: Add 'overlays' to SECTIONS and SECTION_WORDS ("the Overlays"), or make the schema tolerant (`.catch(undefined)`) and let normalize drop bad entries with its existing note.
